steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Breogan... was the owner of that key.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: During Iberia's Golden Age, he became a guest of honor to the aristocrats and nobility. He was once seen as the symbol of the budding harmony between the Ægir Islanders and Iberians.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Nobody knows what he was doing right before the disaster, or what he lacked the time to do. But he had already left behind a significant legacy. And for you, significant directions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Regardless, he is part of the past. I have no doubt you will be the ones to make the choice, here in the present.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As for the key... The question of why Breogan's key was left in Kazimierz is one we do not need answered.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But it was found by the Hunter, Skadi. This was no coincidence, but rather an inevitability. You all have a natural sensitivity towards the sea.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Indeed, I handed the key to that band. You will learn what they truly are. Perhaps the Ægir will need to enlist their help.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They are also searching for answers. Most of them are young, uncomfortable with the ocean's changes. After all, they cannot truly leave the place of their birth.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes... I hope we'll succeed. Humanity faces too many problems, and the layers upon layers of disasters can easily extinguish the light of our current civilization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Gladiia, if you wish to act alone, I won't try to dissuade you. Skadi is just like you. Perhaps all the Hunters are.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But whatever you do, don't think you can solve all of this land's problems by yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Hm? Ask away. I will answer any of your questions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ishar-mla...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Where did you hear that name?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: We're almost there.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But the ocean is just too vast. Even slight inaccuracies in the coordinates can lead to huge errors.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...It is also much calmer than I imagined.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: More than calm. Since leaving the lighthouse, we've actually faced fewer and fewer attacks.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Not even the wind or waves are stirring.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What does it mean?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It means—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Are you nervous, my poor little bird?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Eek! Wh-When did you— Stand where I can see you!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Who are you calling nervous, anyway? It's just... very, very few people manage to make it this far out into the ocean, so I... I can't be sure that—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Nay, your eyes are drawn back to over your shoulder, not to the horizon. You fear loss, more than the unknown.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Your superior gave you this chance so you could board the Stultifera and to reach out to the Ægir, not for you to wallow indecisively.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...I know that.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Before the fight comes to us, you must— Hey. Do you smell that, Shark?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Of course. Keep this cozy little boat slightly to the right, and soon we'll be able to see the bigger boat.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It's long since become yet another nest though. Do we really intend to dive right in?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Do you need to rest, Specter?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Me? Is there something wrong with me? Why would you ask that?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Your hand is shaking.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Hm?
Specter looks down at her hand. The one not wielding a weapon is indeed trembling slightly in the sea breeze.
Her consciousness gradually clears up and plunges deep into the abyss, untouchable.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I... Ah, is this anxiety? Or... excitement?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But why?
Gladiia reaches out and gently holds Specter's hand, with Skadi following suit. The three Abyssal Hunters share a moment of silence.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Welcome home, Hunters.
Gladiia solemnly steps onto the ship's bow.
The sea breeze cleaves a path through the night, carrying upon it a familiar scent.
The quiet vessel sleeps soundly atop the ocean. It is a vassal of the sea breeze, the guest of an era.
Idealism was ubiquitous in that era, and it reflected the peoples' spirit of exploration—as well as their arrogance.
Skadi and Gladiia gaze wordlessly at the ship.
In an instant, they are inundated with a flood of thoughts. But in the end, they are invariably dragged back to the past—their youth, their home, the rhythmic swaying of the ship.
Only Specter continues to grip tightly onto the weapon in her hand, the sea breeze picking up slightly.
This breeze will carry the Hunters home.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithers across a rocky surface)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, burn them.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Screeches)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lord Carmen, we can't afford to stay here much longer. The team of Hunters is in danger.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The Penal Battalion is being held back. It seems even I have underestimated the extent of the Church of the Deep's taint.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We should've cleared a temporary forward base at Gran Faro, to continue the pursuit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We didn't have a choice.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: If we have no way of securing the town, we'll be under attack from both sides.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: An Iberian Tercio consists of at least ten companies, approximately three thousand people. The officers of the Penal Battalion are more than sufficient to lead them to victory.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You seem quite knowledgeable about this.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We've crossed paths more than once.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Are you suggesting we let the Penal Battalion handle Gran Faro, and head straight to the Eye of Iberia?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I wouldn't be opposed to that proposal, were we dealing with Victoria's fleet.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Otherwise, our losses will be even greater.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Miss Frost? Why are you—

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A warm-up workout, she said.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: We come from the sea. We are the sea.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: However... (Riffs dejectedly)

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...If you're willing to help, that would be ideal. What can you offer?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I can make them listen. Listen to my song.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: And your companions?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Apologies in advance, but Dan wants to borrow that chapel. The others are in there thinking up new songs.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Music? Your melodies are considerably different from what I used to hear in Leithanien. Are you sure they'll be interested in this sort of thing?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs tersely)

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: The meaning of life... is music.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I just want to clean up the venue before the show starts.
Frost slowly pulls out her guitar.
Carmen cannot help but be surprised. He can tell that the organism in front of him is truly, genuinely thinking about 'music.' Her words contained no superfluous intentions.

It is by no means a metaphor. Use the word as such, and Frost's attention will quickly wander. She only thinks about music. Only this form of art, capable of stimulating her soul, can hold her attention.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Flinching slithering sounds)

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs experimentally)
The lurking Sea Terrors circle around her. Observing, examining, judging.

They dare not wantonly approach her. They smell a familiar scent. They realize that the guitarist in front of them is a hollow vessel. Her distant connection resonates through the depths bestowed to them as their birthright.
Even on land, they instantly feel as if they have become one with the sea.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Conflicted, confused slithering sounds)

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: How... miraculous.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: These creatures are intimately connected with the land itself. In their eyes, are humans and Sea Terrors no different?
Frost does not answer. She is intoxicated by the melody, consumed by the passion.
Kal'tsit knows that the question was rhetorical.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Kal'tsit, was this also part of your plans? For them to sit on the coast, while the Penal Battalion delves into the sea?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you choose to believe so, then yes.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But the Penal Battalion didn't even have time to prepare even a single ship for us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's already one sitting along the shore.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's been years since the Gran Faro project was scrapped.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...First we must uproot the evil that still grips this land.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I remain an Inquisitor. I will not sit idly by and watch the corruption that's been infesting Iberia slip away, right before my eyes.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Woah!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Are you alright?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: L-Let go of me! Don't just go around picking people up!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But, my fragile little bird, how will you climb up this tall deck if I don't carry you?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Th-That's not what I meant— Tch, forget it...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What's the matter?
Inquisitor Irene simply stares blankly at the scenery in front of her.
A dim sliver of light in front of the pitch-black sea. In front of the ship's mast, time seems to have stood still for the past sixty years.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So this... is the Stultifera. 'Stultifera Navis.' The Ship of Fools.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The flagship that housed both scholars and soldiers, the floating palace of a fallen dynasty. It's quite... different from how it's described in the books.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: W-Wait!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What are you even searching for, on a ship this big?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Breogan was an Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This key must be hiding some sort of clue that the Ægir wanted to leave behind.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: A key? What is it meant to open?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: That's what I'm here to find out.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Even ignoring its size, the ship's also been lost at sea for sixty years. How do you plan to—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Perhaps you young Iberians haven't had much exposure to these transport vessels. Even with Breogan's help, this thing was so shoddily built.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Why you...!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Were the seas calm on our way here? I'm sure you know the answer.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Then my next question for you is this: 'why didn't this ship sink?'

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You don't mean—
Footsteps. Heavy, viscous footsteps.
A shadow appears upon the deck, where no living beings should stir.
No, Irene immediately reprimands herself for having such a thought. Gladiia's question was also on her mind. Along the shore, in the waters. She's already seen so many of these.
The moment she sees the enemy, the young, talented Inquisitor Irene's first instinct is to hold her breath.
By the time she remembers how to breathe, Gladiia has already stepped forward.
(Screeching howl) —!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Interesting, you managed to dodge it.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Not for long.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't even think about it!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It hid inside the cabin! Should we chase it?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Yes, that is where it went.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But why would it hide inside? We're out in the middle of the ocean.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What do we do?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It's not alone. There's more than one Seaborn on this ship. And even more Sea Terrors.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We should split up.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll go after it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'll head down.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: D-Down? How? Do you people already know the layout of this ship?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We don't, but that's nothing a sharp blade can't solve.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Excuse me?! This is the most important legacy of the Iberian sages we're talking about here!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: And where will you go, little bird?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I... I have an obligation to supervise you. So I'll go with you.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: There are so many mysteries shrouding the Stultifera. If it's been preserved this well, why did it never try to return to Iberia in the last sixty years?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: As an Inquisitor, I must uncover the truth.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Shall we hold hands then?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Wh-What's the meaning of this?!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You are a fruit of elegance and grace. But your hard work and natural talents are worthless before the enemies you'll face.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I fear we will lose you with but a momentary lapse of focus.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...You look down on others too much, Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Keep her safe then.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Will do.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Did you remember something?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...The sea breeze told me. It spoke of a sculpture. It is weeping, waiting for me.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Will I be able to find it on this ship?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Of course. But make it quick.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'll be waiting for you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What sculpture?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Well, let us say our greetings to the deceased while searching for its whereabouts, Skadi.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...I'm glad you still remember my name.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: This place... really is fit to be a palace.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But, how is it so pristine? There's not a speck of dust to be found. Look, even the floorboards are sparkling.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Maybe someone wanted to keep it tidy.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Who though?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Who knows.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You said you were going to pursue that monster. How are you planning on doing that?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Its scent doesn't lie.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Though this place is full of putrid smells. There must be more—

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Laborious slithering sounds)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Sea Terrors!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: As expected, they turned this place into a nest.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I'll handle this.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithers around in place)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: —Wait! Specter! The scent's coming from below!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ugh—
Ishar-mla.
Ishar-mla.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Urgh, that impact... Are you alright, Specter?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Specter? Laurentina!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What are you looking at? A mirror? Why is there a mirror?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...The mirror's been broken.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What's with this place? Why did the Iberians make a transport vessel into a palace?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's nothing like Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Is there anything special about the mirror?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I saw it.
At first, there was a speck of light from the surface of the shattered mirror. But it quickly gave way to the dark shadow beneath it. Its eye.
The Seaborn had long been waiting here, sitting alone in its golden hall.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Ishar-mla, La-tina, Louu-tina, Laren-tina......?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's young... No, we can't judge their strength by size. Another Seaborn, without a doubt.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Sea Terrors too! They're gathering, Specter!
Specter ignores her words as she stares blankly at the mirror. And at the Seaborn behind it.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...You remember me?
The Seaborn nods slightly. It looks at Specter and Skadi with confusion. Thinking.
Why are they different from how they were in 'the past'? What happened to them? How can it help free them from their shackles of flesh and blood?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Specter!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't think about it!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I'm not.
Her tone had changed.
Skadi looks at Specter with astonishment. She had never been able to get a definite answer from either Gladiia or Kal'tsit regarding the moment of clarity Specter displayed in Sal Viento.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Laurentina, you...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Laurentina. Yes, Laurentina.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Look, here on the scroll hanging from my weapon. Back when I wrote my name down and hung it here, I could still remember where I was born.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ahhh... A lucid dream, huh? Really, it's been too long.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Specter.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Mm. We can reminisce later.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Whether in Sal Viento or aboard this familiar-yet-unfamiliar vessel, I really hope that next time I'm awakened, it's by Ægir's resplendent domes instead of you ugly monsters.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Hey, thanks for sitting back and letting me finish. Wait, you weren't seriously about to call us your kin were you? Gross.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Come on. Why don't you take a little nap too?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Sink into the quagmire of consciousness, and relinquish the gift of life.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: —– (Screeches)
